core_obligations: Affineness of the disjoint union (proof lines 2185-2204): the definition of a standard covering makes each U_i affine, so the disjoint union V is an affine scheme, which is assertion (1).

The single covering (proof lines 2204-2218): the family {V -> U} is an fpqc covering because V -> U is flat, surjective and quasi-compact, and it is a tau-covering for the topologies other than Zariski, which is assertion (2).

Comparison of Cech complexes (proof lines 2207-2232): the covering U refines V and V refines U, so the two refinement maps between the Cech complexes are mutually inverse, and the complexes agree, which is assertion (3).
proof_roadmap: Use the affineness of the members of a standard covering to see that their disjoint union is affine.
Check that the single morphism from that disjoint union is an fpqc covering and a tau-covering except for Zariski.
Compare the two Cech complexes through the refinement maps in both directions.
difficulty_reason: The lemma replaces a standard tau-covering of a scheme by a single covering with the same Cech complex: the disjoint union V of the members is affine, the one-element family {V -> U} is an fpqc covering and a tau-covering except for Zariski, and the two Cech complexes agree (statement lines 2166-2183). The proof verifies affineness from the definition of a standard covering (proof lines 2185-2204), checks the covering properties of V -> U (proof lines 2204-2218), and compares the complexes by exhibiting refinement maps in both directions (proof lines 2207-2232). The non-formal content is the mutual refinement of the two coverings. The claim is H2: three short verifications.
